annotations.text:
Which numbers are real

400 / 304 / 55 / 84.7% and the 27 + 11 + 3 exclusions come straight from docs/business-definition.md.

Everything else is sample data, shaped to reconcile with those totals: per-carrier late counts sum to 55, counted rows sum to 359, monthly order volumes sum to 400.

Average delivery time shows [N.N] because that figure is not in the docs yet. Carrier names and SKU-1042 demand are invented — swap them for the real dataset values.

Design system: shadcn defaults, untouched

--radius 0.625rem → cards 14px, buttons/inputs/badges 8px, chart bars 6px.
Button and Input h-9 = 36px. Sidebar 16rem = 256px. Header 64px. Page padding 24px, grid gap 16px.

Colors are the literal --chart-1..5 and neutral oklch() tokens, so wiring Recharts to var(--chart-1) reproduces these exactly. Type is Geist; PNG/PDF export falls back to system-ui.

"Show the working" — a side sheet, four blocks

shadcn Sheet, side="right", 480px. The chart stays visible on the left while the working scrolls on the right. Below ~1024px it should go full-width.

1. Filters used — dates, carriers, what was included
2. What was measured — the figure, the formula with real numbers, the breakdown. Only rendered for KPIs and calculated numbers; a plain list answer skips this block.
3. The steps I took — the agent plan
4. Data used — a one-line summary plus the two buttons

Written for the logistics manager, not a developer: no JSON, no field names, no module names.

Reference sheets, not screens.

Left: every chart type inside the full AnswerCard, at the real 900px width, with the shared anatomy spelled out on top and the per-type rules under each card. Build the shell once; these six are just the body.

Right: the layout decision behind the Screens page, with the tradeoff written down.
